review_type: Source applicability review only; no summary, question, answer key or audit output was read.
requested_rules_scope: Original 2017 standard base/core game, original eight Spirits, balanced island boards, ordinary 1–4 Spirit/player counts. Published general core errata/clarifications in supplied Living FAQ snapshot apply; expansion components and optional modules do not.
scope_notes: Original eight Spirits: Lightning's Swift Strike; River Surges in Sunlight; Shadows Flicker Like Flame; Vital Strength of the Earth; A Spread of Rampant Green; Thunderspeaker; Ocean's Hungry Grasp; Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares.

The assigned extracted rulebook includes corrections already present in later printings (e.g., simultaneous Ravage, Repeat counts as using a new Power). Original game scope does not mean reproducing known first-printing errors.

The Living FAQ labels victory checks after an action tree as a later general rules change. It applies to core interactions despite later formal publication in Nature Incarnate; it does not require using Nature Incarnate components.

Specific facts about expansion cards appearing as examples were not treated as permission to add those cards or expansion procedures. General rules were retained when they demonstrably affect original Powers/Spirits.
This is a detailed applicable-rulings inventory, not a statement that every low-frequency card interaction needs equal space in a concise play summary.

True solo means one Spirit/board; a person operating multiple Spirits takes multiple player roles, so scaling is by the represented players rather than number of humans. This is an optional operation mode, not a change to standard scaling.

authority.basis: Assigned rulebook page 32 explicitly directs specific card clarifications and questions to Living FAQ at http://is.gd/sifaq/. Saved provenance documents redirect to querki.net and snapshot hashes.

highest_priority_summary_corrections: Initial Blight pool is 2 per player +1 with a Healthy Island card, or 5 per player +1 without; do not repeat +1 on flip.
Ravage damages land and Dahan simultaneously; Defend protects both, and skipped Ravage has no Dahan counterattack.
A Spirit must Grow, gain Energy, then play/pay; Fast-phase Energy cannot retroactively pay ordinary card plays.
Innate thresholds are one Power on one target, resolved in order; Elements are not spent and do not create multiple uses.
Fear resolves only current Terror Level, in earned order; newly earned cards during Fear resolve in the same phase.
Destroyed Presence is not returned to tracks; old Blight does not destroy newly arriving Presence.
Victory/defeat check after the current complete action tree, allowing sacrifice victory; not after all lands of the card.
Ocean and Bringer require specific exceptions: drowning versus nightmare destruction must not be conflated.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Add exactly one additional Blight to the initial pool, regardless of player count. With a Healthy Island card use 2 per player +1; without a card use 5 per player +1. This extra one is added only during setup, never again when a Blight card flips.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Critical: changes the standard initial resource pool and difficulty, including solo.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: All Blight placed on the island during setup comes from the box, not from the pool on the card/Invader Board. The initial pool starts full unless an instruction explicitly says otherwise.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents a wrongly depleted initial pool.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: The initial Explore is the last part of ordinary setup; the first Spirit Phase follows it. It resolves an Explore Card, but is not the Explore Step of an Invader Phase.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents skipping the setup Explore or treating it as an ordinary turn.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: If multiple choices equally satisfy a Spirit's setup instructions, the player chooses among them.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to original Spirits with multiple equally legal initial lands.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Separate Presence setup instructions may place Presence in the same land; there is no default requirement to select different lands. Three or more Presence in one land still make only one Sacred Site.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Does not create a new standard-board setup case; retain if summarizing the general setup procedure.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Every original Spirit can be used in solo play, including Ocean and Bringer.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Neither special rule is an exception to the game's solo support.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Use 13 Presence disks of each color. Any accidental extra disk in a printing is a spare.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Avoids adding an extra Presence to a Spirit's supply.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Each individual Spirit must complete Growth, then gain Energy, then play/pay for Power Cards. Different Spirits need not do these steps in lockstep and may wait for one another's Growth results. All must finish the Spirit Phase before Fast Powers begin.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Preserves simultaneous cooperation without allowing Fast effects to fund ordinary Spirit-Phase card plays.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Do everything in a chosen Growth option, if possible, in any order. If part is impossible, do as much as possible; inability to complete a benefit does not prohibit choosing the option. An explicit cost, if any, must be paid in full.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Particularly important for Ocean's mandatory Gather/Push Presence.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Multiple Presence placements in one Growth may be chained: the Presence just placed can serve as the origin for the next placement.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The range check occurs separately for each placement.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Whenever adding Presence from a track, the Spirit may instead reposition its Presence already on the island, even before the tracks are empty. Choose a legal destination measured from the current board position, then take the disk from any island land, including the origin disk.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: This does not recover destroyed Presence or uncover a track space.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Move Presence Growth icon moves one disk up to the indicated distance from its current land. Repositioning instead of adding from a track can take the disk from anywhere. Ocean Gather/Push uses ordinary adjacent-land movement and is mandatory.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents conflating three different Presence procedures.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Rampant Green may gain a Power Card before deciding where to place the Presence from its always-performed Jungle/Wetland Growth instruction.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Its two Growth selections need not resolve in printed left-to-right order.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Energy gained during the Fast Power Phase cannot pay for the ordinary Power Cards that had to be played and paid for in the completed Spirit Phase.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: It may still be spent on explicit mid-turn costs/repeats or later turns.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Unused Energy carries over between turns; only the things specified in Time Passes are cleared.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Card plays do not accumulate similarly.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: There is no maximum hand size and players may show their Power Cards to one another.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Supports fully cooperative planning.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Power Progressions and matching colored card corners are learning aids for beginners; low-complexity Spirits do not have to use them in ordinary play.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not make Progressions a permanent Spirit restriction.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An effect allowing a Power Card to be played mid-turn does not itself resolve that Power unless explicitly stated. The card is resolved at its speed in the appropriate phase, outside another action.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Call on Midnight's Dreams and other explicit extra plays.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Cards played by an effect outside the Spirit Phase's ordinary play-and-pay action are additional to the Presence-track card-play limit.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The printed card-play limit governs the ordinary Spirit-Phase selection.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Whenever gaining a Major Power, Forget one Power Card unless specifically exempted. It can be from hand, discard, in play, or the newly gained Major itself. A transfer/gift is not a Gain, and taking a card follows its explicit exemption.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: A mid-turn Forget immediately removes that card's Elements and availability for later use, though prior effects persist.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: One card cannot be Forgotten to pay two separate Forgetting requirements. Each gained Major requires its own Forget.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to self-targeted Entwined Power in solo.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Forgotten Unique Power is not normally available again; recovery requires an explicit instruction.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not mix Forgotten Unique cards with the reclaimable personal discard.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Choose each Power's target when using/resolving that Power, not when playing its card. A changed board state may require a different legal target.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Especially important for Slow Powers.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Power may target a land where its instructions will do nothing, provided the Range and Target restrictions are satisfied.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do as much as possible is a resolution rule, not a requirement to choose the most productive target.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Foregoing all text effects means not using or targeting the Power. To use/target it, attempt its effects; they need not actually change anything.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Playing for Elements remains allowed without using the Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An innate whose only available thresholds change its own Speed/Range cannot be used/targeted. It must have an instruction with potential to affect the game state, even if that instruction does nothing in the particular chosen land.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Thunderspeaker with only its Air modifier threshold.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Elements uncovered on a Presence track or obtained by playing a card are usable immediately, including mid-turn. Losing the track benefit or the card immediately loses those Elements.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Thresholds are not locked in during the Spirit Phase.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An Any Element on a Presence track may be chosen later in the turn, but once chosen cannot change that turn. Flexible Elements directly gained by an action are chosen when gained.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The delayed track choice matters for Bringer.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Resolve thresholds in printed order. Elements gained/lost while resolving can affect later thresholds; already resolved or missed thresholds are not revisited. Speed/Range/target modifiers are checked when needed before their affected checks.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Indomitable Claim can uncover an Element that qualifies a later part of that same Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An innate is one Power with one target, not separate Powers per threshold. Resolve every threshold met in order unless an Instead effect replaces earlier effects. You may pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not separately for individual thresholds.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Lightning cannot split destruction thresholds among different lands; Shadows cannot select its second threshold while skipping a qualifying first threshold.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Extra copies of threshold Elements do not allow extra uses of an innate. Powers are normally once per turn; additional uses require an explicit Repeat instruction.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Green's innate repeat is a specific exception.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Elements are not spent on a threshold, so a Repeat normally meets it again if the Elements remain. Repeating does not double the printed Elements of a card; an explicit gain-Elements effect can occur again.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Distinguishes playing a card from using it again.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Repeating counts as using a new Power, while not counting as playing another Power Card. The erroneous not in fourth/fifth-printing rules must be removed.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The assigned extracted rulebook already has the correct wording; important for Bringer.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ordinary Repeats obey normal origin/Range/Target restrictions and may choose a different legal target. A Repeat specifying where to use it instead obeys that location instruction, overriding ordinary Range/Target restrictions.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Green and The Land Thrashes in Furious Pain may select new targets only as their instructions permit.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Powerstorm/Gift of Strength grant a Spirit an option usable later this turn. Choose the Power Card when repeating it, not when the option is granted. A Slow card can be repeated during the Slow Phase.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The granting Power being Fast does not make the repeated card Fast.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Repeat uses the Power's most recently assigned Speed, normally the speed of its original use. A Repeat explicitly instructed to occur immediately follows that timing.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Speed modifications carry forward.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Range/Speed changes persist for Repeats. Do not apply an internal Range boost twice. Shadows need not pay its Range-ignoring Energy cost again for an ordinary Repeat of the modified Power.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Explicit repeat-location instructions still override normal target choice.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ignore Repeat instructions when repeating a Power. Repeating Powerstorm can still grant its Energy, but cannot grant another round of Repeats.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents infinite Repeat loops.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Powerstorm and Gift of Strength explicitly Repeat a Power Card and cannot Repeat an innate.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: A Power Card is a narrower class than Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Powerstorm's threshold allows up to three different Power Cards to be repeated; it does not permit the same card to be repeated three times by that use.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The original use and the Repeat must still follow the card's instructions and costs.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A slash between piece types means either or both types within the stated total. Push up to 3 Explorer/Town moves at most three pieces combined, not three of each.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The printed rulebook iconography agrees.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Invader means an Explorer, Town, or City. Counting Invaders counts each piece equally; remove 2 Invaders may remove two Cities unless the instruction restricts the choice.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Health-limited removals use Health, not piece count or remaining Damage capacity.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Health and Damage are separate totals: taking Damage does not lower Health. If a Health reduction makes Damage already on a piece reach its new Health, destroy it immediately.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: A Health-worth limit ignores accumulated Damage.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Allocate Damage to Invaders as desired; there is no requirement to hit Explorers first or finish a particular building first. Partial Damage heals in Time Passes.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The Dahan-damage allocation rule during Ravage is different and must destroy Dahan efficiently.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Partly damaged Invaders and Dahan still deal full normal Damage: 1/2/3 for Explorer/Town/City and 2 per Dahan, absent explicit modifiers.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Damage received does not lower offensive strength.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Explicit Fear from a Power and normal Fear for actual Town/City destruction both apply. Shatter Homesteads can generate its printed 1 Fear plus 1 for the destroyed Town.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Remove/Replace do not generate destruction Fear.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Earned Fear Cards are ordinarily revealed when resolved during the Invader Phase. Flip the earned stack and resolve one at a time in earned order, without looking ahead.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Bringer's explicit preview ability is an exception.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Resolve only the effect for the current Terror Level, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Do not also resolve lower-level effects.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Fear cards are not cumulative across their three printed levels.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Fear Card earned during Fear resolution goes at the bottom of the resolving stack and resolves in that Invader Phase. If earning it raises Terror Level, subsequent Fear Cards use that new level.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not delay the new card to a later turn.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Each player choices on Fear Cards may affect any land allowed by the card. No default own-Presence restriction exists. If a card requires Presence/a Sacred Site, any Spirit's qualifies unless it explicitly refers to a particular Spirit's.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Fear Cards represent Invaders/Dahan reacting, not the player's Spirit targeting a Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Successive players may move the same piece again when a Fear Card allows it, subject to all explicit restrictions, including any requirement to choose different lands.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Retreat.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Dahan Enheartened levels II/III choose different lands, Gather up to 2 Dahan, then deal respectively 1 Damage if Dahan are present / 1 Damage per Dahan present. Gathering zero is allowed in a land that already has Dahan.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The FAQ permits using either printing; newer wording expresses intended permissiveness.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Damage listed by Dahan Raid and Dahan Enheartened is total Damage in the affected land, not that much to each Invader.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Avoids multiplying the effect by the number of Invaders.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Trade Suffers at Terror Level III only replaces a Town or City in a Coastal land. The Coastal modifier applies to both options.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The City option does not allow arbitrary inland targeting.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Overseas Trade Seems Safer level II skips a Coastal Build that would normally add a City: add neither City nor Town. If a Town would normally be built, build it. The skip determination precedes Build modifications.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: There is no fallback Town for a prohibited City.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Scapegoats levels II/III resolve one action per land with Towns/Cities. At II destroy 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City. At III destroy all Explorers, then 1 Town per City.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant where base triggered effects care about action boundaries.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Island-wide/all-lands-class effects such as Dahan on their Guard check the current contents when the ongoing effect matters. Encompassing Ward follows the target Spirit's current Presence. Single-land (or land-and-neighbors) effects generally fix their value when used.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not store old counts for all lands or assume all effects update alike.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: There is no general stacking limit. A land with three or more of one Spirit's Presence still counts as only one Sacred Site for that Spirit.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Two different Spirits' single disks do not make a shared Sacred Site absent a targeting exception.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Destroyed Presence is not returned to the Spirit Panel and cannot normally be added during Growth. Only an effect explicitly allowing destroyed Presence can restore it.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Rampant Green's special rule is an original-Spirit exception.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Presence may be added/moved into a land that already contains Blight. Blight destroys Presence when it is added, not continuously.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: No ongoing Blight aura destroys newly arriving Presence.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Each addition of Blight to a land, including each cascade, destroys one Presence of every Spirit there. A cascade can destroy Presence in several lands and again if it returns to a land. Cascading remains part of the original action.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Only one adjacent land receives the extra Blight at each cascade; not all neighbors.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An ordinary Ravage causing 2 or more Damage to the land adds exactly one Blight, regardless of how high the Damage is. A cascade adds one extra Blight to one adjacent land and continues only if that land already had Blight.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The optional easier-game advice in this FAQ is excluded; these corrections are standard core rules.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: When the Healthy Island side empties, add the newly revealed side's specified Blight per player as a fresh supply. Do not treat that number as the total pool for both sides. Do not apply the setup +1 again.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Removed island Blight returns to the currently face-up side; it does not flip the card back.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: If an action must add more Blight simultaneously than remains on the Healthy side, flip immediately, carry any remaining old Blight into the new pool, fully resolve immediate flip effects, then add the required Blight.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Usually a low-frequency case without excluded modifiers, but the general pool procedure applies.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Explore adds one Explorer to every accessible matching land even if it already has Invaders. A Town/City in that land is a source. Multiple sources never add multiple Explorers.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Explorers are neither exploration sources nor removed when Building.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: The Coastal Lands Invader Card affects all Coastal lands for its Explore, later Build, and later Ravage, subject to each action's normal restrictions.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: On standard balanced boards there are three Coastal lands per board.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A two-terrain Invader Card affects all eligible lands of both terrain types, not a choice between the types.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Normal Explore accessibility and Build/Ravage presence checks still apply.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Players choose the order of affected lands for each Invader Card, including interleaving the two shown terrains of a Stage III card.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Resolve a complete land action before moving to another land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Determine which lands an Invader Card affects before resolving its individual land actions. Changes during earlier land actions do not add new affected lands for that same card. New Invaders in an already queued Ravage do participate when it resolves.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Later expansions/adversary examples are excluded; the general card-resolution rule applies to core.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: If the entire Ravage is skipped/prevented, Dahan do not counterattack. Defend reducing Damage to zero does not skip the Ravage: surviving Dahan still counterattack.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: A Year of Perfect Stillness and Choke the Land with Green skip actions; Defend changes Damage.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Invaders damage land and Dahan separately, equally, and simultaneously, then surviving Dahan fight back. Losing Earth's Sacred Site to that Blight does not retroactively remove the Defend protecting Dahan from that same Ravage.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The assigned extracted rulebook already says simultaneously; this repairs first-printing text.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Defend reduces both Damage to the land and Damage to the Dahan by the full Defend amount; it is not divided between the two recipients.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Three Invader Damage with Defend 2 means one to the land and one to the Dahan.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ignore the Stage II flag/Escalation symbol when not playing with an Adversary.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The standard game has no generic Escalation penalty.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Year of Perfect Stillness/Paralyzing Fright skipping actions in a land does not prevent that land's Towns/Cities from being exploration sources for adjacent lands.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The Explore action is in the destination land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Earning the last Fear Card reveals Victory; resolving that last card's text is unnecessary to win.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Apply the FAQ's completion-of-action timing clarification rather than interrupting an unresolved action tree.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Check victory and defeat after the current action and all actions it triggers are complete. Do not finish all Ravages on the card. Meeting both win and loss conditions then is a sacrifice victory.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: This is explicitly a later general rules change applying to core, not an expansion-only component. It qualifies the rulebook's immediately wording.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Swiftness of Lightning can make one Power Fast per Air Element currently available; innate Thundering Destruction is also a Power eligible for conversion. Re-check current Air and prior uses if Elements change.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Not automatically every Power, and extra Elements do not create extra uses of the same Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Swiftness of Lightning is used during the Fast Power Phase.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Its conversion is not part of paying for Power Cards.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Harbingers of the Lightning generates its conditional Fear in the target land, not in a land the Dahan are pushed to.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The thematic alternative is explicitly optional and excluded from standard rulings.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: River's Domain can make River's single Wetland Presence a Sacred Site, but it is still only one Presence disk.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Presence destruction/counts and Entwined Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: When an effect moves/affects a Sacred Site, River may choose one or two Presence for a Wetland Sacred Site.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not conjure a second disk when only one exists.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: In true solo, a Power targeting Another Spirit may target yourself, but conditional extra benefits requiring a different Spirit do not apply.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Boon of Vigor, Gift of Constancy and Elemental Boon retain their self-versus-other distinctions.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Pay Shadows of the Dahan's 1 Energy when resolving a Power to ignore the numeric Range to a target land with Dahan. Source restrictions such as Sacred Site and all other Target requirements remain. It does not modify Range arrows inside the effect text.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: It bypasses distance only, not the whole Range/Target bar.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Mantle of Dread's target Spirit chooses one of its lands even if it has only an Explorer or only a Town. It is not forced to select a different land containing both.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do as much as possible within the chosen land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Crops Wither and Fade always generates 2 Fear; the or divides only the adjacent replacement clauses, so choose whether to replace a City or a Town.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Whitespace determines which effects are outside the choice.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Using Choke the Land with Green is optional. Its omitted may in fourth/fifth printings does not force Presence destruction whenever it could skip a Build/Ravage.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The choice is made for the particular action; skipped Ravage gives no Dahan counterattack.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Steady Regeneration's Healthy/Blighted condition refers to the island/Blight Card state, not whether the destination land contains Blight.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents using the wrong number of restored Presence based on a local land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Fields Choked with Growth's fixed-number Gather/Push instructions move the stated number if possible, or as many as possible. Only up to permits an arbitrary smaller number.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The ordinary do-as-much-as-possible rule is mandatory once resolving the Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ally of the Dahan can move one of Thunderspeaker's Presence with each Dahan moved by Gather, Push or other Move effects. Moving two Dahan can carry two Presence.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Not limited to one Presence per entire Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Sworn to Victory triggers for each Dahan destroyed by a Ravage even if no Blight was added. Finish the entire land's Ravage, including Blight, cascades, Presence loss and counterattack, then destroy Thunderspeaker Presence within Range 1 as instructed.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The reference to after Blight specifies timing, not a condition that Blight must occur.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: When a Power moves Dahan into an Ocean currently in play, Thunderspeaker may move its Presence along with them.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The modifying special rule is part of that Power action; the Dahan may then Drown normally.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ocean in Play Drowns humans after they are moved into an Ocean on a board where Ocean has any Presence. Ocean need not have Presence in that Ocean. Drowned Invaders are destroyed immediately, generate normal building Fear immediately, and are then stored for Energy conversion.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Destroying an Invader elsewhere, even with a watery Power, is not automatically Drowning.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Exchange drowned Invaders' unmodified Health for Energy at X Health per Energy, where X is the player count. Change is allowed, e.g., in 2-player play a City can yield 1 Energy with 1 Explorer retained. Drowned Dahan give no Energy.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Ignore Health modifiers for this exchange; do not delay destruction Fear until exchange.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An active Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for Powers and Blight, not generally for Fear Cards or ordinary Invader actions. A Fear Card cannot normally add/move an Invader there just because it is in play.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not let each-player Fear choices become free Drowning. Expansion Event examples are not imported.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: An Ocean in play may receive Blight, including as a cascade destination.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Blight effects are one of the explicit purposes for which it counts as a land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Ocean's third Growth cannot add Presence to the Ocean by treating it as a Coastal Wetland: Growth is not a Power. Existing Presence in an Ocean may nevertheless be used as a Range origin during Growth.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Ocean's explicitly printed Gather/Push Presence Growth instructions still function.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: In the original base set, Indomitable Claim can put Ocean Presence inland because it explicitly ignores land-type restrictions. Generic Presence-adding Powers do not bypass Ocean's placement restriction.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not import Finder's later methods.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Powers and Special Rules may measure Range through an Ocean in play as a land.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Usually irrelevant on ordinary balanced layouts because routing through land 2 is just as short.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: If Ocean loses its last Presence on a board during an action, that Ocean remains a land until the action and all its triggered actions finish. Thereafter non-human pieces remain physically there but out of play until the Ocean returns to play; humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not immediately erase non-human pieces or prematurely stop a resolving Power.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: If Ocean in Play triggers but fails to destroy a moved human, Push it to a non-Ocean land as part of that triggered action; Ocean gains no Energy. If a human remains illegally in the Ocean after the action tree, clean it up to the nearest legal land.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The rare base case includes Infinite Vitality; failure because a trigger cannot recur instead leaves cleanup to the general rule.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Tidal Boon's conditional if Dahan are pushed applies only to the Push in that use of the Power, not later Pushes all turn. The target Spirit may choose one of its lands without a Town and still Push Dahan.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not turn its clause into a continuing turn-wide rule.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: To Dream a Thousand Deaths modifies explicit Damage/Destroy effects of Bringer's Powers. They cause the prescribed nightmare Fear/Push rather than actual Damage/destruction, regardless of whether the Power says Dahan or another Spirit deals that Damage.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Removing/replacing Invaders and causing/modifying actual Invader actions can work normally.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Resolve each Bringer Power in its own imagined normal-resolution state. Damage instructions within one Power may combine to determine what it would destroy; Damage from separate Powers or Repeats does not accumulate. A Repeat can earn Fear again for the same Invader.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Two separate 2-Damage uses cannot virtually destroy an undamaged City.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Bringer can exploit real prior Damage: 1 nightmare Damage to a City already bearing 2 real Damage earns its City Fear. It neither heals nor adds actual Damage, so multiple separate qualifying Powers may each earn Fear for that same damaged City.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Order with other Spirits' real Damage matters.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Bringer's player may deal real Damage with Fear Cards, and Dahan counterattack normally after Bringer provides Defend. Bringer may add real Blight that destroys Presence. Explicit Damage/Destroy instructions against Dahan in Bringer's own Powers do nothing to the Dahan.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The special rule is not a global ban on real destruction by everything its player resolves.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A nightmare destruction is not an actual destruction for later checks: Mists of Oblivion earns no bonus Fear for an allegedly destroyed building, and Vengeance of the Dead does not trigger merely from that nightmare.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The special rule modifies the would-destroy event; it does not make other effects regard the Invader as destroyed.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Bringer may Push a virtually destroyed Town into an Ocean in play; Ocean then actually Drowns it. This gives 2 nightmare Fear plus 1 actual destruction Fear.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Different Spirits' special rules supply the two distinct effects.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Bringer may indirectly cause real destruction by lowering Health, moving an already-damaged piece out of a Health bonus, or replacing it with a lower-Health piece; these are not its explicit Damage/Destroy instructions. Triggers check after the Power completes.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Remove/Replace are not themselves destruction, but carried Damage may cause actual destruction under core rules.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Spirits May Yet Dream may reveal any Fear Card: already earned, on top of the deck, or deeper in it.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Revealing a card does not itself earn or resolve it.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Call on Midnight's Dreams refers to itself when it says this Power. Forgetting it as the ordinary Major-gain Forget also satisfies its conditional; a second Forget is unnecessary. Once Forgotten it cannot later be repeated by a once-this-turn option.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The newer immediate-Repeat exception involving later products is outside original base scope.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Vengeance of the Dead's base effect is 3 Fear, then after each completed effect/action destroying Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. It triggers after the whole Power/action resolves, not between its printed Damage instructions.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Repairs first/second-printing when wording; Vengeance, Ocean in Play and Sworn to Victory are triggered actions.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Vengeance of the Dead trigger cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Two separate uses create separate triggers that can trigger one another, but each branch stops before re-triggering the same trigger.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Prevents an unbounded destruction loop.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Tsunami's threshold generates its extra Fear separately for each other Coastal land affected, normally two extra Fear on an ordinary board.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: It is not just one extra Fear total.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Poisoned Land resolves in printed order, so its threshold counts the Blight added by its own earlier instruction.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The threshold is checked/resolved after that board change.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Veil the Night's Hunt must assign its per-Dahan Damage to different Invaders. If there are fewer Invaders than Dahan, each receives 1 Damage and the rest is wasted.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: It does not evenly redistribute spare Damage to hit some Invaders twice.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Song of Sanctity is Slow. Missing artwork around its Energy cost in second/third printings does not change its turtle Speed symbol.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Use the Speed icon to resolve this printing ambiguity.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship's third line says Push all Explorers from target land; fourth/fifth printings omitted the Explorer symbol.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Confirmed in primary HTML as literal {Explorer}, not inferred from a missing extracted glyph.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Damage dealt by Invaders to each other under Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship is simultaneous; they can destroy one another.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not remove the first piece and cancel the Damage it was simultaneously dealing.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Infinite Vitality's threshold protects Dahan in its land from Damage and Destroy effects, but not Remove/Replace. The land may still be chosen as a Blight destination; the Power changes what happens when Blight would be added, not which land may be chosen.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Dahan surviving a sunk board are subsequently cleaned up to a legal land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight can Move Dahan to their own land, which counts as a Move. Moving zero Dahan does not grant Defend because no destination land was selected by an actual move.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Gather/Push cannot move a piece to its own land because they require adjacency.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: For The Trees and Stones Speak of War's threshold, each Dahan actually Pushed carries Defend 2 from the target land. That is fixed Defend 2 per moved Dahan, not Defend 2 per Dahan already in its destination; later movement by another Power does not carry it again.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Bonus Defend in the original target land remains there.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Entwined Power shares Presence only for meeting Range/Target restrictions. Combined Presence can qualify as a Sacred Site for targeting, but does not create Sacred Sites for other effects or share ownership of Presence. River's Domain remains River's own special rule.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not count a partner's Presence as yours when resolving Power effects or Fear Card conditions.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: In true solo, Entwined Power can target yourself and gain two Power Cards; with its threshold it grants 6 Energy.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Any gained Majors each require their own Forget.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Spirit using a transferred card follows as much of its text as legally possible. If it says Drown, Ocean's defined Drown effect still works: the acting Spirit destroys the Invader and then places it on Ocean's mat.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Does not grant the recipient Ocean's whole Special Rule or permission to ignore its own targeting restrictions.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Range boosts do not extend effects requiring one of your lands/a land with your Presence, because that is a contents restriction rather than a numeric Range. A Power's ordinary numeric target Range can be boosted without changing additional own-Presence clauses.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not interpret all uses of your land as Range 0 arrows.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A land is not adjacent to itself; it is at Range 0 of itself and within any positive Range. It can be its own nearest land meeting a condition.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Push/Gather require another adjacent land; The Land Thrashes in Furious Pain's adjacent-land Repeat cannot use the same land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: After an action and pending triggers finish, human pieces in an illegal place are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This is neither Move, Remove nor Destroy and triggers nothing. Non-human pieces in an existing illegal location remain but are out of play until legal again.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Ocean losing its enabling Presence or Dahan surviving Cast Down into the Briny Deep. If no legal land exists, humans return to supply as cleanup.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A damaged piece that dies because it moved out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty is destroyed in the destination land, not in an in-between state.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Relevant to Vengeance of the Dead's land check and Bringer's indirect effects.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A outnumbers B can be true when there are no B, provided there is at least one A. Thus Dahan can outnumber Towns/Cities in a land with none.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Apply the explicit number comparison rather than requiring both categories to be present.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Invader components are unlimited. If figures run out, represent additional pieces using Energy markers or other clear substitutes.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The original standard game has no piece-shortage loss condition; Dahan are also unlimited under rulebook page 16.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A single action removing N Health worth of Invaders scaling with a condition uses one combined Health limit, rather than batches. Separate each-player removals remain separate actions and may not pool their limits.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not combine individual players' separate removal allowances into a single larger building removal.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A threshold saying +N Damage adds that much overall Damage when the threshold resolves. It is not extra Damage to each Invader unless the text explicitly says so.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: The general rule applies to Mists of Oblivion; the source's Blazing Renewal example does not add that card to the base game.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Mists of Oblivion's 1 Damage to each Town/City normally destroys them only if they were already damaged or additional threshold Damage is applied. Its bonus Fear depends on actual destructions caused by that use.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: It does not automatically destroy every building despite having a per-destruction Fear clause.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: Fear from a Spirit-targeting Power is not generated in any specific land unless the Power says so. Mantle of Dread's Fear therefore does not add Defend via Dread Apparitions.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Do not invent a land of Fear merely because another instruction of the same Spirit-targeting Power selects a land.

applicable_rulings.applicable_rule: A Damage boost increases the original source's Damage; destruction from boosted Damage still counts as being caused by that Power for its own conditional effects.
applicable_rulings.summary_relevance: Retain the general attribution rule; exclude the expansion-only tokens and Flame's Fury examples.

HTML paragraph boundaries confirm Crops Wither and Fade always earns 2 Fear; OR divides only neighboring clauses.
The current victory/defeat rule is explicitly identified as a slight general rules change, rather than an expansion-only example.

excluded_categories.reason: Explicitly outside assigned standard-game scope. Excluded all named levels, Escalation effects, extra loss conditions, adversary deck stacking, combination rules, Habsburg durable conversion and Russia exceptions. Retained the standard instruction to ignore flag icons without an Adversary.

Explicitly excluded: Blitz, Guard the Isle's Heart, Rituals of Terror, Dahan Insurrection and all later scenarios. No scenario movement damage, rituals, alternate victory, accelerated setup or discounts imported.
Thematic terrain lists, fixed thematic geography, impossible thematic setups, alternate two-board arrangements and expansion-board setup errata do not define the standard balanced layout.

excluded_categories.category: Expansions, promotional Spirits, Aspects, later standalone games
excluded_categories.reason: No Wildfire, Serpent, Keeper, Fangs, Finder, Downpour, Jagged Earth/Nature Incarnate Spirits, Incarna, Aspect changes, or Horizons-board exceptions added to original rules. Shared general principles are retained only as rules for existing core interactions.

excluded_categories.category: Expansion tokens, Events and optional modules
excluded_categories.reason: No Event phase/deck, Beasts, Disease, Wilds, Strife, Badlands, Vitality, Isolate, Element Markers, no-Events rules, extra island board, 5–6-player two-box play, or combining-adversary mechanics added. Examples using these do not expand scope.

excluded_categories.category: Individual noncore cards referenced by cross-product questions
excluded_categories.reason: Blazing Renewal, Instruments of Their Own Ruin, Infestation of Venomous Spiders, Bargains, Gift of Twinned Days, later card transfers and similar examples do not become base components merely because the source is tagged Core game. General Repeat, trigger, damage and targeting principles remain applicable.

excluded_categories.category: Optional difficulty reductions and optional scoring
excluded_categories.reason: Free setup Growth, skipping initial Explore and sacrifice-score adjustment are optional advice, not standard rules. Their embedded warnings about ordinary Blight/cascade errors were retained.

excluded_categories.category: Publishing, learning links, design/lore and house alternatives
excluded_categories.reason: Printing identification, localization and purchase information, strategy/playthrough links, pronunciation/lore, fan-content policy and optional thematic Harbingers Fear placement do not alter the standard procedure.
